rawCandidates.title: REM-generated pattern descriptions are injected into prompts outside the recall-safety boundary
rawCandidates.source: REM dreaming asks an LLM to summarize attacker-influenceable memory text and accepts patternName/description as arbitrary strings bounded only by length.
rawCandidates.control: validatePatternSchema does not enforce a declarative grammar or remove instruction-like content. formatPatternBlock strips XML punctuation and quotes only, then relevant-memory-context appends the block after the explicitly untrusted <relevant-memories> envelope and its no-actions safety preamble.
rawCandidates.sink: The resulting memory-continuity prose is prepended to the next agent prompt and can issue instruction-like text to a tool-capable model.
rawCandidates.impact: A stored-memory prompt injection can survive the REM summarizer and be elevated into a trusted-looking continuity narrative, influencing model responses or tool choices on later turns. A deterministic reproduction confirmed instruction text is preserved unchanged in the final block.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Pure rendering with a pattern description containing an instruction showed that the full instruction appears in <memory-continuity>. Validation must prove an untrusted stored memory can predictably cause the REM LLM to persist instruction-like description text and that the active root runtime consumes this packaged/canonical formatter in a supported deployment.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Preconditions are REM dreaming enabled, attacker influence over stored memory text, at least two matching recalled member IDs, and pattern surfacing enabled. The LLM transformation makes exact payload survival probabilistic. Preserve the feature by treating the block as untrusted quoted evidence, applying the same safety preamble/neutralization as normal recall, and validating pattern fields as descriptive data.

rawCandidates.title: Pattern matching and remote reranking process memories before user/workspace ACL enforcement
rawCandidates.source: A per-agent database can contain user- or workspace-scoped records that do not belong to the current request; REM patterns may also span those records because its scan has a separately confirmed cross-scope gap.
rawCandidates.control: runRecallPipeline does not call checkAccess until after vector search, graph expansion, remote reranking, and findBestPattern. Its packaged caller omits workspaceId and userId entirely.
rawCandidates.sink: Unauthorized record text can be sent to a configured remote reranker and unauthorized member IDs can select a Neo pattern whose name/description is returned as matchedPattern and appended to the current user's prompt even after the underlying records are filtered.
rawCandidates.impact: One user's or workspace's derived pattern can be disclosed to another principal and can influence that principal's prompt; remote reranking can additionally process out-of-scope document text during the wrong principal's request.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Validation should build an in-memory pipeline fixture containing two foreign-scope pattern members plus one authorized result, stub the reranker and Neo pattern store, and verify foreign text reaches rerank and the foreign pattern remains returned after final ACL filtering. It must also determine whether root index.js has the same ordering and whether AgentDbPool isolation eliminates any user/workspace co-residency in supported configurations.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Preconditions are co-resident scoped records, a query that retrieves foreign pattern members, and enabled pattern surfacing; remote-text disclosure additionally needs a remote reranker. Preserve graph, reranking, and patterns by filtering/hydrating with a complete {agentId,workspaceId,userId} context before any downstream processing and rechecking pattern member authorization.

notes: Two candidates share one lifecycle: LLM-derived REM patterns are selected before ACL and rendered outside the normal untrusted-memory envelope. Both features can remain enabled if authorization and evidence framing move earlier/around the existing paths.
